label: early original-phase steps (t=2-4) after a "c" has appeared
explanation: Fires during the original-input phase at positions t=2..4 (a weak tail at t=5) once the letter c has appeared earlier in the sequence. It is strongest when c is the first token or the first tokens are c c (top activations: c c c then the next token, around 7.9), and it decays a step or two after the c, and as the c moves later. The current input token barely matters. It almost never fires at t=0-1, at t>=6, on the delimiter (0.4% of mass), or in the copy phase. It does not fire in sequences with no c. False positives are mostly at t=4-5 when the c came at position 2 or later, and some activation goes unexplained on later c-free steps.

issues: Reproduced the reported test scores for the original predicate: P 0.743, R 0.889, F1 0.810, mass recall 0.966.

Systematic false-positive class: the predicate counts any c seen before the step, but a c that first appears at position 3 almost never triggers the feature. For (t==4)&(orig(3)==c) with no earlier c, precision is 0.142 (12,437 predicted). At t=5 it is 0.019. This is about a third of the predicate's 34k test false positives. The predicate should require the c to be among the first three tokens.

Timing is graded by how long ago the c was, and the predicate ignores this. When c is the first token (c at 0, not at 1): precision is 1.00 at t=2, 0.98 at t=3, 0.555 at t=4 and 0.054 at t=5. When c first appears at 1: 0.70 at t=2 (the very next step), 0.99 at t=3, 0.86 at t=4, 0.22 at t=5. When c first appears at 2: 0.60 at t=3, 0.68 at t=4, 0.20 at t=5. So the feature peaks 2-3 steps after an early c. The step right after the c is weaker, and so is a lag of 3 or more when the c was first.

Claims that check out: zero firing at t=0-1, a weak tail at t=5 (t==5 & seen c has precision 0.106 and 2.4% of mass), essentially nothing at t>=6, delimiter 0.4% of mass, copy phase about 0 (19 steps), the input token itself matters little, the top activations are on c c openings, and c-free sequences hold only 0.4% of mass (precision 0.003).

The explanation partly admits the false positives ('mostly at t=4-5 when c came at position 2 or later'), but the predicate and label do not encode it. 'After a c has appeared' overclaims: a late c (position 3+) does not count.

Refined predicate: c within the first three positions and already seen, t=2..4. Test P 0.806, R 0.873, F1 0.838, mass recall 0.962. That is better than 0.810 at about the same mass recall. The remaining false positives are mostly the weaker lag-1 steps (e.g. 'q c [r]') and lag-3 when the c was first.
skeptic.revised_label: original-phase steps t=2-4 shortly (mostly 2-3 steps) after an EARLY c (c among the first three tokens)

final_label: original-phase steps t=2-4 shortly (mostly 2-3 steps) after an EARLY c (c among the first three tokens)
